learning_outcomes.text: Analyze signals and systems to interpret machine behavior.
Create transfer functions and signal flow diagrams for technical systems.
Apply Fourier and Laplace transformations as well as digital signal processing techniques to mechanical engineering processes.
Recognize and apply the link between measurement technology and system theory.

Understand and apply practical methods of data-driven analysis, especially concerning measurement data from machines: statistical evaluation, visualization, simple model building and interpretation using common industrial software.
Design filters for signal processing and evaluate their effect.
Record machine measurements and calculate essential machine parameters (power, efficiency, torque, mass forces, speed uniformity). Monitor machine processes using suitable measurement procedures.
Numerically simulate and analyze machine models.
Perform metrological analysis of heat pumps and explain their significance for the energy transition.
Prepare test reports according to industrial standards and systematically document measurement procedures.
Identify and classify the right tools for practical methods.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Measurement Technology
Concepts: Measurement uncertainty, measurement accuracy, calibration
Measurement chain: Sensors, signal conditioning, data acquisition
Signal processing in the context of measurement systems in mechanical engineering
Connection of measurement technology and system theory
Fundamentals of Signals and Systems
Classification of signals
Linear and nonlinear systems
Time-invariance and system description
Signal flow diagrams and their interpretation
Fundamentals of Data Science
Classification and typing of technical data (continuous, discrete)
Cleaning technical data (e.g., outliers, smoothing, gap handling)
Visual representation of measurement data (e.g., time series, histograms, spectra)
Basic statistical quantities (mean, variance, standard deviation, correlation)
Feature extraction from signals (peak detection, frequency components, parameter formation)
Simple regression models for describing technical relationships
Application of industrial software for implementing the mentioned methods
Machine Science: Calculation and Analysis of Machines
Introduction to working and power machines
Calculation of power, efficiency, and energy flows
Investigation of mass forces and their metrological detection
Metrological analysis of torques and speed uniformity
Mathematical modeling of machines
Differential and difference equations for mechanical engineering processes
Application of transfer functions in machine analysis
Numerical simulation techniques (Matlab/Simulink)
Fourier and Laplace transformations in machine analysis
Time and frequency domain analysis
Application of Fourier and Laplace transformation to technical systems
Frequency response analysis of machines
Digital signal processing and sampling
Sampling theorem and value discretization
Digital filtering
Introduction to fundamental industrial measurement procedures
Strain gauges
Bridge circuit
Piezoelectric measurement technology
Acquisition of force, torque, displacement, acceleration, pressure, temperature, speed
A/D conversion
Digital storage and representation of measurement signals
Power brakes
Consumption measurement and exhaust gas analysis
Recording of dynamic vibration forces
Calibration of a pressure sensor
Transient recorder
Recording of vibration accelerations
Engine test bench
Investigation of an internal combustion engine
Vehicle chassis dynamometer
Measurement of tractive force
Piston air compressor
Recording of pV diagrams
Metrological analysis of a heat pump
Metrological determination of engine efficiency (efficiency measurement) on electrical machines using the example of a separately excited DC machine and a three-phase asynchronous machine
assessment_rules: Two written module examinations, each 60 minutes long, are required. Successful completion of the laboratory exercises is a prerequisite for taking the examinations.
